1.heading: AM 3560, BC 444 Title
refs: This Psalm, which was probably composed by Ezra, is another of the alphabetical Psalms: it consists of twenty-two parts, answering to the number of the Hebrew letters
every part being divided into eight verses, and each verse beginning with that letter which forms the title of the part
that is, the first part of eight verses with א, the second with ב, etc. It is an elegant, important, and useful composition
the chief subjects of which are the excellence of God's laws, and the happiness of those who observe them.
